section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Alaska, between which dates are studded tires legally permitted on public roads?
options: a:September 15 – April 30,b:October 1 – April 15,c:November 1 – March 31,d:October 15 – May 1
note: Alaska law permits studded tires from October 1 through April 15. Using studded tires outside this window can result in a fine because studded tires damage dry pavement when not needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Alaska?
options: a:13,b:14,c:15,d:15 and a half
note: Alaska allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 14, one of the youngest permit ages in the country. The permit requires supervised driving with a licensed adult before advancing to a restricted license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers age 21 and older in Alaska?
note: Alaska, like all U.S. states, sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Reaching 0.08% is itself grounds for a DUI charge, regardless of apparent impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Alaska's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.01%,c:0.02%,d:0.04%
note: Alaska applies a true zero tolerance standard for drivers under 21 — any measurable amount of alcohol in the system is illegal. An underage driver with any detectable BAC faces license revocation and criminal penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an icy Alaska road and feel your rear wheels begin to slide. What should you do?
options: a:Brake firmly and steer straight,b:Accelerate to regain traction,c:Steer in the direction of the skid and ease off the gas,d:Turn the wheel sharply in the opposite direction of the skid
note: When your vehicle begins to skid on ice, steer gently in the direction the rear is sliding and ease off the accelerator. This technique — called counter-steering — helps straighten the vehicle. Braking during a skid usually makes it worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Alaska during a whiteout blizzard with near-zero visibility. What is the safest action?
options: a:Use high beams and maintain speed to exit the storm quickly,b:Pull off the road safely, turn on hazard lights, and wait for conditions to improve,c:Follow the taillights of the vehicle ahead closely,d:Drive on the shoulder to avoid the main travel lanes
note: In a whiteout, the safest option is to pull completely off the roadway, turn on your hazard flashers, and wait for conditions to improve. Following another vehicle in a whiteout is dangerous because a chain-reaction crash can occur if the lead vehicle stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on Alaska highways in winter, which of the following actions is most important before beginning your trip?
options: a:Carry at least half a tank of fuel,b:Check the DOT Alaska 511 road conditions report,c:Ensure you have an emergency kit with extra clothing, food, and a shovel,d:All of the above
note: All three precautions are essential for Alaska winter driving. Remote highways can leave you stranded for hours; fuel, road condition awareness, and emergency supplies are each critical for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most residential streets in Alaska when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Alaska's default speed limit on residential and business district streets where no limit is posted is 25 mph. On rural highways without posted limits, the default is higher — always check posted signs to be sure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a state-specific rule about vehicle equipment that applies in Alaska but NOT in warm-weather states like Hawaii?
options: a:All tires must be the same brand,b:Studded tires are permitted during designated winter months,c:Chains are prohibited on paved roads,d:Snow tires must be removed by April 1 regardless of conditions
note: Studded tires are allowed in Alaska from October 1 through April 15 to provide traction on snow and ice. This rule is Alaska-specific; many warm-weather states prohibit studded tires entirely because they damage dry pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Stop completely and yield before proceeding,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:The signal is broken — treat as a 4-way stop,d:Do not enter the intersection
note: A flashing yellow light is a caution indicator. You must slow down and proceed carefully but are not required to come to a complete stop — unlike a flashing red, which requires a full stop.

question: What is the minimum license suspension period for driving without valid liability insurance in Alaska?
options: a:60 days.,b:Two years.,c:90 days.
note: In Alaska, if you are involved in a crash while uninsured or fail to show proof of liability insurance when required, your driver license can be suspended for at least 90 days. States use license suspension to enforce mandatory insurance laws and to ensure that drivers can pay for damages they may cause.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Alaska, what must you do when a school bus stops and activates its flashing red lights on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop only if you are driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 15 mph and pass with caution,c:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus until lights stop flashing,d:Yield only to children crossing directly in front of the bus
note: Alaska law requires vehicles traveling in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. You may not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm retracts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a yield sign. What does Alaska law require?
options: a:Stop completely regardless of traffic,b:Slow down and yield to cross traffic; stop only if necessary,c:Maintain speed and merge when safe,d:Flash your headlights to signal your intention
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and give the right of way to cross traffic or pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to avoid a conflict, but a full stop is not required when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving at night and see a moose on the road ahead. You should:
options: a:Honk continuously to scare the moose away and accelerate to pass quickly,b:Flash your high beams and proceed carefully,c:Slow down immediately and wait for the moose to move — do not attempt to pass around it,d:Swerve sharply around the moose in the opposite lane
note: Moose collisions are extremely dangerous in Alaska and frequently fatal. Slow down immediately and wait patiently for the moose to move. Honking can startle moose into unpredictable behavior, and swerving risks a rollover or head-on collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the required following distance in normal driving conditions under Alaska's safe driving guidelines?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Alaska recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On icy or slippery roads — common in Alaska — that gap should increase to 6–10 seconds or more to account for longer stopping distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a right turn at a red light in Alaska?
options: a:Never — right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:After a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, unless a sign prohibits it,c:At any time if no vehicles are visible,d:Only between the hours of 6 AM and 10 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Alaska after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic. Some intersections post 'No Turn on Red' signs — always check for those signs before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What shape and color is a regulatory sign in Alaska?
options: a:Yellow diamond,b:White rectangle or white circle,c:Orange rectangle,d:Green rectangle
note: Regulatory signs — such as speed limits, stop signs, and no-passing zones — are typically white rectangles (or white circles, like railroad advance warning) and convey rules you must obey. Yellow diamonds are warning signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving uphill on a steep Alaska mountain road and your engine begins to overheat. What should you do?
options: a:Continue driving and open the windows to let the engine cool,b:Turn on the heater to draw heat away from the engine and pull over when safe,c:Rev the engine to maintain coolant circulation,d:Immediately stop in the travel lane and call for help
note: Turning on the heater pulls heat from the engine coolant into the cabin, which can temporarily reduce engine temperature on steep grades. Pull over safely as soon as possible and let the engine cool before opening the hood — a hot radiator cap can cause serious burns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Alaska, what does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted when the road is clear,b:Passing is prohibited — do not cross the line to pass,c:The road ahead has a sharp curve,d:Passing is allowed only at speeds over 45 mph
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line prohibits passing by crossing that line. Only a dashed yellow line on your side indicates passing is permitted when safe. These markings apply in Alaska and nationwide.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches from any direction, Alaska law requires you to:
options: a:Speed up to the next intersection and turn off the road,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed,d:Move to the left lane and reduce speed
note: Alaska law requires you to pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has fully passed before resuming travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching an intersection where a traffic light has gone dark (no lights showing). How should you treat it?
options: a:Treat it as a yield sign — slow down and yield,b:Treat it as a 4-way stop — come to a full stop and take turns proceeding,c:Treat it as a green light if the intersection looks clear,d:Stop only if you see other vehicles approaching
note: A dark or non-functioning traffic signal must be treated as a 4-way stop in Alaska and nationwide. All drivers must come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn based on order of arrival and right-of-way rules.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: You must be especially alert for motorcycles because they are smaller and harder to see than cars, especially in blind spots, at intersections, and in heavy traffic. Their size also makes it harder to judge their speed and distance, so you should check mirrors and blind spots carefully and give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop at the stop line when present.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if there is no stop line or crosswalk.,d:Continue if the way appears clear.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, you must stop at that line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk, and if there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only proceed when the light turns green and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your destination in heavy city traffic, you should:
options: a:Back up in traffic to reach the destination.,b:Make a sudden U-turn in the road.,c:Stop immediately in the lane.,d:Continue to the next block or use the next legal turn to return.
note: If you miss your destination in heavy city traffic, you should keep moving with traffic and go to the next block or the next safe, legal place to turn around. Backing up, stopping suddenly in a lane, or making a sudden U‑turn can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

question: What is true about smoking or preparing to smoke while driving?
options: a:It is recommended on long trips to stay awake.,b:It does not affect driving abilities.,c:It helps you stay alert and improves driving.,d:It is a distracting activity and can reduce driving safety.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that divides your attention increases your risk of not noticing hazards and reacting too slowly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,b:You must merge into the indicated lane.,c:You may turn left if you first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means the turn is permitted, but not protected. You may turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the crosswalk. Make the turn only when the way is clear.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian follows right-of-way laws.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,d:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against a signal. You are required to use extra caution around pedestrians and must do everything you reasonably can to avoid hitting someone, regardless of who technically has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass if it is safe to do so.,c:No passing is permitted.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles traveling in either direction may cross the line to pass when it is safe and legal to do so, and when there is no oncoming traffic close enough to create a hazard.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A public recreation area.,b:A nearby school zone.,c:There is an existing or possible driving hazard ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to existing or potential hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or work zones. Most are yellow, while orange diamonds are used in construction and maintenance areas.

question: At a railroad crossing where the signals are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Look for a train,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Stop and look for a train.
note: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must come to a complete stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped while the warnings are active. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing and you are sure no train is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Slow and prepare to stop.,b:Stop and check oncoming traffic.,c:Turn without yielding to pedestrians.,d:Proceed through when the road is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never means you can ignore pedestrians or other right‑of‑way rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:By driving off the pavement.,b:If the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is a clearly marked lane or enough space on a paved roadway to do so safely. You must never pass on the right by driving off the pavement or on narrow bridges where there is not enough room.

question: When traveling to an area you don't know well, what should you do before you start driving?
options: a:Depend on road signs to find your way.,b:Begin with only a general idea of your destination.,c:Plan your trip in advance.
note: Before driving in an unfamiliar area, plan your route in advance. Knowing your turns, exits, and alternate routes reduces last‑second lane changes, sudden stops, and distractions from trying to navigate while driving.

question: Which of the following is a known effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Faster,b:Improved coordination.,c:Loss of concentration.
note: Alcohol slows brain function and affects judgment, concentration, vision, and coordination. Even small amounts make it harder to focus on the road, react to hazards, and control the vehicle smoothly.

question: What does a traffic signal showing a solid red arrow require you to do?
options: a:Stop and do not turn in the direction indicated by the arrow until the arrow turns green.,b:Stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.,c:Turn slowly in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow. You must remain stopped until the arrow turns green or a permitted signal appears, and only then may you proceed if it is safe.

question: If convicted of DUI in Alaska, what is the minimum period your license may be revoked?
options: a:30 days,b:60 days,c:At least 90 days
note: In Alaska, a first DUI conviction or refusal to take a chemical test results in a driver’s license revocation for a minimum of 90 days. More prior offenses lead to longer revocation periods, but the minimum for a first offense is at least 90 days.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action should drivers take when approaching a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Turn on their headlights.,b:Proceed through the intersection with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not need to stop, but you must be alert for cross traffic, pedestrians, and any hazards before continuing.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark the edges of a crosswalk. What is true about pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.,c:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
note: At marked crosswalks, pedestrians have the right-of-way. Drivers must yield and, if necessary, stop to allow pedestrians already in the crosswalk, or stepping into it, to safely cross the roadway.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what precautionary steps should you take?
options: a:Try to drive around any lowered gate if you are in a hurry.,b:Speed up to cross before any gates lower.,c:Look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop until it is safe to cross.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train. Cross only when you are sure it is safe and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Because you are traveling faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass
note: You must be cautious when passing a bicyclist because you are moving into or near the oncoming lane and other drivers may not expect this. Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and the bicyclist may need extra space to avoid hazards. Always pass only when it is safe, with plenty of room and clear visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter an intersection and the traffic light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and back up.,b:Accelerate.,c:Stop as quickly as possible if you can do so safely.
note: When a green light turns yellow as you approach, you must stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, continue through with caution. Never back up in an intersection, and do not speed up to beat the red light.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Stay calm and move out of their way.,b:Flash your lights and confront them.,c:Call the police immediately from the roadway.,d:Speed up to retaliate.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and avoid any actions that could escalate the situation. Safely slow down, increase your following distance, and move out of their way. Do not confront, signal aggressively, or try to retaliate; your goal is to create space and reduce risk.

question: Why should you pump the brakes on a vehicle that does not have ABS when slowing on a slippery surface?
options: a:To keep air out of the brake line.,b:To prevent the tires from wearing out faster.,c:To help prevent the wheels from locking and avoid skids.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, firmly pumping the brakes on a slippery surface helps prevent the wheels from locking. Locked wheels slide instead of rolling, which reduces steering control and can cause a skid. By pumping the brakes, you allow the tires to regain traction between brake applications so you can better steer and slow down.

question: How should you drive when visibility is reduced by fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use high beam headlights to better illuminate the road.,c:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
note: In fog, reduce your speed and drive cautiously because you cannot see as far ahead and hazards may appear suddenly. Use low beam headlights so you can be seen and see the road; high beams reflect off the fog and make visibility worse. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe driving.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The alcohol will negate the drug’s effects.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be increased.,d:They always cancel each other out.
note: Combining alcohol with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and loss of judgment. The effects of both substances can be stronger together than either one alone, which makes driving much more dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you turn your front wheels when parked facing downhill?
options: a:Pointed straight ahead.,b:Aiming any direction.,c:Turned toward the curb or shoulder.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb or edge and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To reduce the chance of being struck from behind, you should:
options: a:Stop frequently to prevent tailgating.,b:Brake harder than usual to create distance.,c:Keep pace with surrounding traffic within the legal speed limit.,d:Drive noticeably slower than surrounding traffic.
note: To reduce the chance of being hit from behind, drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit and leaving a safe following distance. Sudden braking or driving much slower than surrounding traffic can surprise other drivers and increase the risk of rear‑end collisions.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Decreases your field of vision.,b:Has no effect on vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:Increases your field of vision.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you see less to the sides, which is called "tunnel vision." This makes it easier to miss pedestrians, cyclists, and cross traffic, so you must scan more actively and avoid driving faster than conditions allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane roadway when you see a Merging Traffic sign, you should:
options: a:Honk at entering traffic to warn them.,b:Stop to let merging cars in.,c:Always maintain your current speed regardless of others.,d:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over if no one is beside you.
note: On multi‑lane roads, help merging drivers by adjusting speed and, when safe and clear, moving over a lane to give them space. Cooperating with merging traffic keeps traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the risk of side‑swipe and rear‑end collisions.

question: Under ideal driving conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Six seconds.,b:Four seconds.,c:500 feet.
note: Maintain at least a four‑second following distance under ideal conditions; increase the gap when conditions worsen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels straight and your turn signal on. If you are hit from behind with your wheels turned left, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight lets a rear‑end impact push you forward instead of into opposing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:As far to the left as possible.,b:Close to the right side of the street.,c:In the nearest passing lane.,d:Near the center of the street.
note: To make a right turn safely, move your vehicle as close as practicable to the right edge or curb before turning. This reduces the chance of another vehicle passing on your right and helps you turn into the correct lane without swinging wide or cutting across lanes.

question: When you are on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Cross under no circumstances.,b:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, driveway, or side road.,c:Cross to pass other vehicles when there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may not cross them to pass other vehicles. You may cross them only when making a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road, and only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the road?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe to do so.,b:Brake hard and sharply turn back onto the road.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road and wait.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking. Keep steering straight while you slow down, then when your speed is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: Which of the following best describes a “No zone”?
options: a:A lane with restrictions on speed.,b:The blind spot area around large trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be unseen.,c:A designated no-passing zone on two-lane roads.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots around trucks and buses where the driver cannot easily see smaller vehicles. Staying out of these areas helps avoid collisions because the truck or bus driver may not know you are there.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter remedies (all of the above).,b:Only marijuana.,c:Only cold remedies.
note: Any drug that affects the brain or body can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter remedies. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving after taking any medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing only.,b:Merging traffic ahead.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians and being ready to stop if needed. It does not require a full stop unless other conditions make it necessary.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Stay at the scene and report the collision as required by law; if you cannot locate the owner, also leave your contact information on the vehicle.,b:Leave immediately since you tried to find the owner.,c:Call your insurance agent and then leave without leaving your information.,d:Leave a written notice with your name, address, contact information, and an explanation of the collision in a secure, visible place on the vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop and leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle. The note should include your name, address, contact information, and a brief description of what happened, and you must report the crash as required by local law.

question: Which statement about alcohol’s effect is correct?
options: a:Alcohol does not affect memory.,b:Only long-term heavy drinking affects driving skills.,c:Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration and judgment.,d:Only a BAC greater than the legal limit affects concentration.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reactions and reduce concentration, judgment, and perception. You can be unsafe to drive even if your BAC is below the legal limit.

question: What does Alaska require concerning license plates on most vehicles?
options: a:No specific license plate requirement.,b:Two license plates (front and rear).,c:A single license plate mounted on the rear of the vehicle.
note: Alaska generally requires most vehicles to display a single license plate mounted on the rear of the vehicle. The plate must show current registration tabs and be illuminated so it can be read from a reasonable distance at night.

question: Why is the road often extra slippery during the first half hour of rain?
options: a:Tires have not yet absorbed the water.,b:Dust and oil on the road have not yet washed away.,c:Water tends to pool the most at the beginning of a rainfall.
note: During the first part of a rainfall, water mixes with oil, grease, and dust that have built up on the road surface. This creates a slick film that greatly reduces tire traction until enough rain falls to wash these substances away, making the road especially slippery in the first 10–30 minutes.

question: Approaching a school bus with flashing red lights, what must a driver do?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the bus’s red lights stop flashing and it is clearly safe to proceed.
note: Drivers must come to a complete stop for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm; do not attempt to pass.

question: What is the only reliable way to sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Drinking black coffee.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Exercising vigorously.,d:Waiting for your body to eliminate the alcohol.
note: The only way to become sober is to allow time for your body, mainly your liver, to process and eliminate the alcohol from your system. Coffee, cold showers, food, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Assume others will yield to you.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for an opening.
note: When entering an interstate from an entrance ramp, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Never force your way in or stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic or signals require it, because stopping there can create a rear‑end collision risk.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, you should:
options: a:Try to squeeze through quickly.,b:Split the difference and pass both at once.,c:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,d:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When you face hazards on both sides, do not try to pass between them at the same time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first so you can then move away from the bicyclist with plenty of space. Handling one hazard at a time greatly reduces the chance of a collision.

question: Which of these is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving slightly slower than traffic.,b:Using signals consistently.,c:Maintaining a steady lane position.,d:Weaving between lanes.
note: Weaving between lanes is a classic sign of impaired driving. Alcohol and drugs affect coordination and judgment, causing drivers to drift or swerve in and out of their lane, make sudden corrections, and drive unpredictably. Always increase your following distance and report a suspected drunk driver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals must be used for any movement left or right that could affect other road users. This includes changing lanes, turning at intersections, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from a curb, driveway, parking area, or alley. Signaling early and clearly lets others know what you intend to do so they can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal shows a green arrow for your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the circular green light appears.,b:Stop.,c:Turn in the direction indicated by the arrow when the intersection is clear.,d:Proceed straight through the intersection.
note: A green arrow is a protected signal that allows you to turn in the direction of the arrow; oncoming traffic and conflicting movements are stopped by a red light. You still must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection and complete the turn only when the path is clear.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to?
options: a:A roadway with volume restrictions on stereos.,b:The large blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The "No-Zone" is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck or bus driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working because of a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: a:Park and wait in the intersection for power to be restored.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark due to a power outage, you must treat the intersection as a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn: first vehicle to stop goes first; if you arrive together, yield to the vehicle on your right. Always proceed with caution and be prepared for other drivers who may not follow the rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle whose driver sounds the horn first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps avoid confusion: always check for traffic from your right and be prepared to let that vehicle go first.

question: Which action helps prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before braking.,b:Always check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,c:Sound your horn before braking.
note: To help prevent rear‑end collisions, avoid sudden, hard braking whenever possible. First ease off the accelerator to let your vehicle begin to slow, then apply smooth, steady brake pressure. This gives drivers behind you more time to see your brake lights and react safely.

question: Which behavior describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,b:Drives slowly at all times.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: A good defensive driver constantly scans the road and watches the actions of other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. By anticipating what others might do and spotting hazards early, you have more time to adjust your speed, change lanes, or stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and continue through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop as if at a stop sign
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over the others?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.,d:A flashing yellow light.
note: If a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s directions even if they conflict with traffic lights, signs, or pavement markings. Officers can override normal controls to keep traffic safe and moving, and their instructions are legally binding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multilane highway, slower traffic should:
options: a:Drive in the left lane.,b:Drive in any lane.,c:Drive in the right lane.,d:Drive on the shoulder to let traffic pass.
note: On multilane roads, slower traffic should keep to the right lane so faster vehicles can pass safely on the left. This reduces lane changes, prevents tailgating, and helps traffic flow smoothly.

question: When may you legally use parking lights?
options: a:When visibility is poor.,b:Within one hour of sunset or sunrise.,c:When a vehicle is parked.
note: Parking lights are intended only to make a parked vehicle more visible; they are not bright enough for driving. When the vehicle is moving in low‑light or poor‑visibility conditions, you must use your headlights, not just parking lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: When leaving a driveway or alley and entering a street, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb line and yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic. Enter the roadway only when it is safe, even if you have been stopped for a while.

question: Which distraction increases a driver's risk of a crash the most?
options: a:Playing a CD.,b:Listening to the radio.,c:Using a cell phone while driving.
note: Using a cell phone while driving, whether handheld or hands‑free, creates visual, mental, and often manual distraction at the same time. This greatly increases crash risk compared with simple activities like listening to the radio.

question: If another car might hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Turn on emergency lights instead of horn.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Flash your headlights only.,d:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when you think they may not see you and could collide with you. The horn is your primary audible warning device; use it briefly to alert others, not to express anger.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:Visibility is reduced and you cannot see as well.,b:Traffic moves faster at night.,c:There is more traffic at night.,d:Headlights make it easier to judge distances.
note: At night, darkness greatly reduces how far and how clearly you can see, making it harder to spot hazards, judge distances, and see pedestrians or animals. Because visibility is reduced, you must use extra caution, slow to a safe speed, and use your headlights properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as necessary. A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The driver may suddenly open a door as you pass, so use extra caution.,b:The driver will wait until you pass, so speed up.,c:The parked car will not move, so slam on your brakes.
note: When passing a vehicle that is parked or just pulled up to the curb, assume someone may suddenly open a door or pull out into traffic. Slow slightly, keep extra space if possible, and be prepared to brake to avoid hitting an opening door or a person stepping out.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,c:Potential driving speeds for the area
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must never drive faster than the posted limit, and you must slow down below the limit when road, traffic, or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use hand or mechanical turn signals?
options: a:Only after you start the turn.,b:For a minimum of 100 feet before turning or changing lanes.,c:Only in city traffic.,d:Only when there is traffic behind you.
note: You must signal before you turn or change lanes so others have time to react. In most areas you must signal for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes, and at higher speeds you should signal even earlier so drivers have more time to see and respond.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance work ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A railroad crossing ahead.
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for construction, maintenance, and work zones. They alert you to road work, lane shifts, workers or equipment on or near the roadway, and other work‑related hazards so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:All railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.,b:You never need to stop for a crossing.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
note: You must always obey railroad crossing signals and gates. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train. Not all crossings have lights or gates, so you must also look and listen carefully whenever you approach tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your right and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, garage, or alley, you must stop if necessary and yield to all traffic and pedestrians already on the road or sidewalk. At an unmarked intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right, not the other way around.

question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
options: a:Never use your horn.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate your intentions with other road users.,d:Only drive on back roads to avoid traffic.
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users know what you plan to do. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and, when needed, your horn to communicate your intentions to drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians so they can adjust and avoid conflicts.

question: If you are driving inside another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind a vehicle that the driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are driving in another driver’s blind spot, you should either move ahead or drop back so that you are clearly visible in their mirrors. Staying in a blind spot increases the risk that the other driver will change lanes into your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Only if you can see at least 200 feet on either side.
note: When there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic. This lets you obey the stop requirement while still being able to see cross traffic safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a recommended speed.,c:The exact speed to avoid tickets.,d:The minimum required speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a target or guaranteed safe speed. You must slow down below the limit when conditions such as rain, fog, traffic, or road work make the posted speed unsafe. It is also not just a suggestion; it is legally enforceable.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.,b:Keep your high beams on until they dim theirs.,c:Glance toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams are blinding you, avoid looking directly into the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane markings as a guide until the vehicle passes. This helps preserve your night vision and keeps you in your lane.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Pump the accelerator repeatedly.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Drive faster to get past puddles quickly.,d:Slow down and make sure tires are properly maintained.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce the risk, slow down on wet roads, especially where water pools, and keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread. High speeds, sudden moves, and worn tires all make hydroplaning more likely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using sirens or flashing lights?
options: a:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if the emergency vehicle is behind you.,c:Only when other drivers yield first.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, if possible, until the emergency vehicle has passed. This applies whether the vehicle is in front of you, behind you, or approaching from any direction.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed after a train passes?
options: a:Start across as soon as the first train passes.,b:Follow the car ahead immediately regardless of view.,c:Cross quickly without looking.,d:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.
note: At crossings with multiple tracks, one train can hide another. After a train passes, do not start across immediately. Wait until the gates are fully raised (if present) and you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions to be sure no other train is coming before you proceed.

question: When near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Force the motorcycle to give up lane position.,b:Allow the motorcycle a full lane to itself.,c:Share half of your lane with the motorcycle.,d:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd or share the lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle. Give them the entire lane width so they have room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest method?
options: a:Slow down until no oncoming traffic is present, then pass while leaving plenty of space.,b:Keep driving; the bicyclist must get out of your way.,c:Wait until the next traffic signal or stop sign to pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist on a two‑lane road, slow down and wait until there is no oncoming traffic so you can move over safely. Pass only when you can leave plenty of space—at least 3 feet where required by law, and more at higher speeds—then return to your lane once you are well clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the common maximum speed limit on most Alaskan roadways unless posted otherwise?
options: a:60 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:50 mph.
note: On many Alaskan highways, the general maximum speed limit when no sign is posted is 55 mph. Always follow posted signs, as lower limits apply in areas such as school zones, business districts, and residential neighborhoods, and some major highways may have higher posted limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:Either lane.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you must turn into the nearest lane going in your direction of travel. This usually means entering the leftmost lane of the one-way street if you are turning from the left lane of your road. Turning into the closest appropriate lane helps prevent conflicts with traffic in other lanes.

question: Which of the following DOES occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:You become more alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance improves.,d:You recover from headlight glare faster.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time, makes it harder to judge speed and distance, and reduces alertness and visual ability. Because of this, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: A driver approaching a stopped school bus with flashing amber lights must:
options: a:Sound their horn and pass slowly.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the bus has passed.
note: Flashing amber (yellow) lights on a school bus mean the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children. You must slow down and be ready to stop. When the red lights flash and the stop arm is extended, you must stop and remain stopped as required by your state’s law.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Pass with caution.,b:Do not pass.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not legally pass other vehicles from your lane. It is used where passing would be especially dangerous, such as on hills, curves, or areas with limited visibility.

question: On long trips, what is an effective way to prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Slow down and drive more slowly.,b:Turn up the car radio volume.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: On long trips, the best way to prevent drowsiness is to stop regularly to rest, walk, and stretch. Short-term tricks like turning up the radio or just slowing down do not keep you alert and are not safe substitutes for real rest.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,c:Do not immediately use your brakes.
note: In a tire blowout, ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, avoid hard braking, and let the vehicle slow gradually. Once under control and speed has decreased, steer smoothly to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean you should do?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,b:Stop if you can safely do so; a red arrow is coming.,c:You may complete the turn without yielding.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and a red arrow will appear. You should stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, complete the turn with caution.

question: Who is required to wear seat belts under Alaska law?
options: a:Only passengers under 16 are required.,b:Only front-seat occupants are required.,c:Everyone in a moving vehicle is required to wear a safety belt.
note: Alaska law requires every person in a moving vehicle to use a safety belt or appropriate child restraint. The driver is legally responsible for ensuring that passengers under 16 are properly restrained.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a crash, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait for law enforcement before moving the vehicle.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: After a minor crash, if there are no serious injuries and the vehicles are drivable, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to a safe location. This helps prevent additional collisions while you exchange information and assist anyone who is hurt.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the left side mirror.,b:Look quickly over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,d:Turn on your hazard lights first.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. This over-the-shoulder check reveals vehicles in your blind spot that you cannot see in your mirrors.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle before proceeding.,b:Always yield the right-of-way,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,d:Require pedestrians to yield to vehicles.
note: Drivers must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians and do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting them, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly. Pedestrians are vulnerable road users, so drivers must slow down, be alert in crosswalks and near intersections, and yield the right‑of‑way whenever there is any doubt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a driver's left arm extended upward indicate?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver plans to stop.
note: Hand and arm signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and a left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. A left arm extended upward therefore indicates the driver intends to turn right.

question: How should you position your wheels when parking downhill on a two-way street?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left away from the curb.,b:Keep the wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the right toward the curb.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb. If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will hit the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signal is working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:Honk to get the officer’s attention.,b:Follow the officer’s directions.,c:Follow the traffic light signals.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s instructions even if traffic lights or signs show something different. The officer’s directions override signals and signs to keep traffic flowing safely in special situations such as crashes, road work, or power outages.

question: Which statement describes distracted driving?
options: a:It is very uncommon.,b:It is extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone on the road.,c:It is harmless in light traffic.,d:It is only a problem for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, such as texting, eating, or adjusting controls. It greatly increases the risk of crashes and endangers you, your passengers, and others on the road, so you should always stay focused on driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you always do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling lets other road users, including those you may not see, anticipate your actions and helps prevent collisions.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,b:When it approaches you with no red lights or stop arm displayed.,c:If you are on a two-lane highway and the bus’s red lights are flashing and/or its stop arm is extended.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and is loading or unloading children. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn left.
note: Hand signals are used if your turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm extended downward with the palm to the rear means the driver is slowing or stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you not do?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Fail to check for drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. Failing to check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane is dangerous and can cause a collision.

question: When you see an approaching vehicle with flashing red or blue lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue driving with caution without stopping.,c:Continue driving until the next intersection before stopping.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes, it decreases BAC.,b:No, it has no effect on BAC.,c:It cancels the alcohol effect.,d:It speeds up alcohol elimination.
note: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). It may make you feel more awake, but the alcohol is still in your system and your driving ability remains impaired. Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC.

question: What are the consequences of refusing a requested chemical test by law enforcement?
options: a:The DMV will take administrative action against your driving privileges, such as suspension or revocation.,b:You will only receive a warning.,c:There are no administrative consequences.
note: Under implied consent laws, if you refuse a lawful chemical test (breath, blood, or urine), the DMV will take administrative action against your driving privilege, often including a mandatory suspension or revocation. In many states, the refusal is also recorded on your driving record and can lead to additional penalties in court.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular road signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones ahead.,b:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells you to slow down, be prepared to stop, and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle require a longer stopping distance?
options: a:On dry, paved highways.,b:On a wet, icy, or otherwise slippery road.,c:On any road at night, regardless of conditions.
note: Your vehicle needs a much longer distance to stop on wet, icy, or otherwise slippery surfaces because your tires have less traction. Reduce your speed and increase your following distance whenever the road is wet, icy, or covered with loose material. Nighttime can make it harder to see hazards, but it does not by itself change the friction between your tires and the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through it without stopping. If traffic ahead is blocking the intersection, wait behind the stop line or crosswalk until there is enough space to clear the intersection completely. Blocking an intersection is unsafe and often illegal.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road that is divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:Traffic travels in two directions (a two-way road).,c:It is a one-way road.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic flows in both directions and you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so. Yellow lines always separate traffic moving in opposite directions; broken segments indicate that passing is permitted if you can complete it safely without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow together with a red light, what movement is allowed?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,b:You may proceed straight ahead only.,c:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, even if the main signal is red. You may proceed only in the direction the arrow points, after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection. You may not go straight or turn in any other direction until those signals allow it.

question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to brake gently and avoid sudden steering or speed changes, which helps prevent loss of control.

question: Under what circumstances may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To pass another car.,c:To turn into a driveway.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either side. You may cross them only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley, or to enter or leave a roadway where it is specifically allowed, and only when it is safe.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, when must you pull over and stop?
options: a:Regardless of your direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights and siren approaches, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of whether it is coming from ahead or behind. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Roll down your window and ask someone for directions.,b:Get off at the next exit and safely return to the missed exit.,c:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep driving to the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the highway or shoulder, as this is extremely dangerous and usually illegal. Exit at the next opportunity, then find a safe route back to your intended exit.

question: How can you best avoid the risk of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Tell people you won't drink if offered.,c:Call a taxi after you start drinking.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive at all. Plan a sober driver, use transit, or arrange a ride in advance. Once you have started drinking, your judgment is already impaired, so relying on decisions made after drinking is unsafe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Only when following a motorcycle.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view of the road ahead.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes following large vehicles that block your view, driving in bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions. More space gives you extra time to react to hazards ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are about to miss your highway exit, you should:
options: a:Signal,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit ramp.,c:Stop in the lane and wait for a gap to reverse course.,d:Continue to the next exit and leave the highway safely.
note: If you are about to miss your highway exit, continue to the next exit and leave the highway safely. Never stop in a travel lane, back up on the highway, or reverse on the shoulder. Sudden stopping or reversing on a freeway creates a serious crash risk for you and other drivers.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,b:Not drive if you are tired.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:All of the above.
note: Safe night driving includes several habits: make sure your headlights and taillights work and are properly aimed so you can see and be seen, avoid driving when you are tired because fatigue slows your reactions, and increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react in the dark.

question: If your turn signals fail, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use your horn,b:Use hand signals,c:Use your headlights
note: If your electrical turn signals are not working, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or change lanes. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up at the elbow for a right turn, and bend your left arm down at the elbow to indicate slowing or stopping.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines indicate?
options: a:A residential district is ahead.,b:A dangerous curve is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you must not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: Which passing rule is correct?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet and make sure no oncoming traffic before passing.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car before returning to your lane.,c:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.,d:None of the above.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Also check mirrors and blind spots and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before turning must you signal your intention?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet
note: On most roads, you must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes so other drivers have time to react. At higher speeds, such as on highways, you should begin signaling even earlier to give extra warning, but the basic minimum distance in many states is 100 feet.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Use only high beams so others see you.,c:Turn off all lights to avoid glare.,d:Leave low-beam headlights on and use emergency flashers.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, keep your low‑beam headlights on and activate your emergency flashers. Low beams and hazard lights make your vehicle visible to other drivers without creating excessive glare, reducing the chance of a collision.

question: After passing a vehicle on a two-lane road (one lane each direction), when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if planning to turn left.,b:When there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,c:Immediately,d:Only after signaling for 500 feet.
note: After you pass on a two-lane road, you should not move back into the right lane until there is a safe space between your vehicle and the one you passed. A common rule is to wait until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and have enough distance to return without making them slow down.

question: About how long does it take, on average, for the effects of one 12‑ounce beer to be processed?
options: a:One hour.,b:45 minutes.,c:30 minutes.
note: A standard drink—such as a 12‑ounce beer, a 5‑ounce glass of wine, or a shot of 80‑proof liquor—takes about one hour for the average body to process. This can vary with weight, sex, food, medications, and other factors, so you can still be impaired even after an hour.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You will not see the road markings.,b:It increases your fuel efficiency.,c:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.,d:You might miss the vehicle's signals.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, greatly reduces the time and distance you have to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance—at least the 3‑second rule in good conditions—gives you enough space to see hazards and stop smoothly.

question: If someone has been drinking, what will help them overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Only the passage of time will reduce alcohol impairment.,b:Hot coffee will sober them up quickly.,c:Fresh air will remove the alcohol from their system.
note: Once alcohol is in the bloodstream, only time allows your body to break it down. Coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air may make someone feel more awake, but they do not reduce blood alcohol concentration or restore safe driving ability.

question: When approaching pedestrians on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Only if they are in marked crosswalks.,b:Yield and be ready to stop as they walk or cross the roadway.,c:Only if a traffic light is yellow or red.,d:Only if they signal you to stop.
note: Drivers must always use caution around pedestrians. Slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop for people walking on or crossing the roadway, whether or not they are in a crosswalk or obeying signals. Pedestrians are vulnerable road users, so the driver has a high duty of care.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as what sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the intersection, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat posted advisory or speed restriction signs in poor road conditions?
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy or snowy conditions.,b:They are only recommendations and do not apply in adverse weather.,c:Reduce speed below the posted advisory when conditions make it unsafe to follow it.
note: Advisory speed signs show the recommended maximum speed for ideal, dry conditions. In rain, snow, ice, or other poor conditions, you should slow down even more and drive below the advisory speed if needed so you can maintain control and stop safely.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens to your abilities?
options: a:Your judgment improves.,b:Your reaction times slow down.,c:Your metabolism speeds up.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, your reaction time slows, your judgment gets worse, and your coordination declines. This makes it harder to notice hazards, make good decisions, and react quickly to avoid crashes.

question: If you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You have space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,c:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
note: When crossing railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle before you start across. Never stop on the tracks and never pass other vehicles while on or approaching the crossing.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:The time between drinks.,d:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how fast your body processes alcohol. A standard drink contains about the same amount of alcohol whether it is beer, wine, or liquor, so the type of beverage by itself does not change your BAC—what matters is the total amount of alcohol you take in over time.

question: You are presumed to be driving under the influence if your BAC is at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.10 percent.,d:0.08 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, a driver age 21 or older is presumed legally under the influence when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is 0.08% or higher. At or above this level, you can be arrested and convicted of DUI even if you feel fine, because your driving ability is significantly impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to stop or park along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you turn on your emergency flashers.,b:To consult a map or directions.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: On freeways, the shoulder is for emergencies only, such as a breakdown, medical emergency, or when directed by law enforcement. It is not legal to stop on the shoulder just to read a map, use your phone, or rest, even if you turn on your hazard lights.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Low-beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: In fog, always use low‑beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare.
