High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them together with low beams for better visibility.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to look?
options: a:Turn your head and body to look out the rear window.,b:Use only the rearview mirror.,c:Open the door and step out to look.,d:Turn on your headlights and back using mirrors only.
note: When backing up, you should turn your head and upper body to look directly out the rear window so you can clearly see behind your vehicle. Mirrors alone do not show everything and can hide children, pedestrians, or objects in blind spots.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, you must:
options: a:Continue at the same speed to clear the way.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Drive with your hazard lights on.,d:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling over to the nearest edge or curb of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can get through quickly and safely.

question: What do round road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Construction ahead.,b:An upcoming railroad crossing.,c:A no-passing zone.,d:A school zone.
note: Round (circular) warning signs are used to indicate an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see a round railroad advance warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, and that vehicle is to your right, you should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and force the other to stop.,b:Speed up to beat the other vehicle.,c:Honk to assert the right-of-way.,d:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and let the vehicle on your right go first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you cannot pass safely unless which condition is met?
options: a:You are traveling below the posted speed limit.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead, passing is not prohibited, and you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle is small enough to pass quickly.
note: On a two-way, two-lane road, you may only pass when you have a clear view of the road ahead, there are no signs or pavement markings prohibiting passing, and you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. Never begin a pass if you cannot safely return to your lane in time.

question: If your vehicle's power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area to stop.,b:Turn off the ignition immediately and continue steering.,c:Open your hood and stop in the lane of travel.
note: If power steering fails, the steering wheel will be much harder to turn, but you can still steer. Hold the wheel firmly, steer with extra effort, slow down gradually, and move to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Do not turn the ignition to the lock position while moving, as this can cause loss of steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet prior to the intersection.,b:After slowing down enough to see cross traffic but not stopping.,c:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and verifying it is safe to proceed.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe.

question: What colors are used on warning signs for upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a white background,b:White letters or symbols on a blue background,c:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
note: General warning signs that alert you to upcoming hazards are typically yellow with black symbols or lettering. These signs warn about curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other potential dangers ahead so you can adjust your driving in time.

question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line adjacent to your lane, you may:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If traffic is clear.,c:If you are on an expressway.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means passing is allowed only on the side with the broken line. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. If the solid line is on your side, you must not pass.

question: An orange triangular sign with red borders displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicates what?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle is broken down.,c:The vehicle is a school bus.
note: An orange triangular sign with red borders on the rear of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, so you should approach with caution and be prepared to slow down.

question: When you approach a steady green arrow signal, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:Make the turn indicated by the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,c:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may make the turn if you are in the proper lane, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you should:
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic you are entering.,b:Always stop before proceeding.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.,d:Accelerate to merge quickly.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the roadway you are entering. Proceed only when it is safe; a full stop is required if traffic or pedestrians are present.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and before crosswalks to show drivers exactly where to stop at a red light, stop sign, or for pedestrians.

question: How does night driving compare to daytime driving?
options: a:It is neither more nor less dangerous.,b:It is more dangerous.,c:It is less dangerous.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you can see less distance ahead, it is harder to spot hazards, glare from headlights can reduce your vision, and there are often more tired or impaired drivers on the road.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians use?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the left side of the road, facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and react if a driver does not see them.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If the gate appears to be malfunctioning.,b:If you think you have enough time to cross before it lowers fully.,c:Never — do not drive around lowered gates.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. A train can approach faster than it appears, and it takes a long distance to stop, so you must wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

question: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle should you dim your high beams?
options: a:400 feet,b:500 feet,c:200 feet
note: To avoid blinding oncoming drivers, you must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within about 500 feet. This distance gives both drivers enough time to see clearly and react safely.

question: What should you do to maximize safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk around the vehicle and check behind it for children, pets, and small objects that may be hard to see from the driver’s seat. Mirrors and cameras have blind spots, so physically checking the area before you get in maximizes safety.

question: Statistics show alcohol is:
options: a:Rarely involved in any traffic crashes.,b:Involved in almost half of all traffic crashes that result in death.,c:The cause of all traffic crashes.
note: Alcohol is a major factor in fatal crashes. In many states, including Alaska, alcohol is involved in a large share of traffic deaths, often around half. It is not involved in all crashes, but it is far from rare in serious and fatal ones.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect driving?
options: a:It distracts you and impairs lane control and vehicle handling.,b:It helps you focus on driving.,c:It has no effect on driving.,d:It makes you a better driver.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your eyes and attention off the road. This distraction makes it harder to maintain steady lane position, react to hazards, and control the vehicle smoothly, increasing crash risk.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that only has a crossbuck and no gates or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until a flagger clears you to cross in all cases.,b:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,c:Turn down your radio to listen for a train but otherwise proceed.
note: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are a police officer.,b:They are signaling for a taxi.,c:They are likely blind and need right-of-way and assistance.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired. You must yield the right-of-way, use extra caution, and be prepared to stop well in advance so they can cross safely without being startled or endangered.

question: What is the minimum jail term for a first-time DUI conviction in Alaska?
options: a:Three days,b:10 days,c:20 hours
note: In Alaska, a first DUI conviction carries a mandatory minimum of three days in jail, along with fines and other penalties. Knowing the minimum helps you understand that even a first offense has serious consequences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Sound your horn to warn others.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.,d:Reduce your speed to below 10 mph.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your rearview and side mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Signal, make sure the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly without slowing abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:Be in the center of the street.,b:Be in the right lane of the street.,c:Be in the left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, start from the left lane of the two-way street and turn into the left lane of the one-way street, the lane closest to you. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles in other lanes.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do with the steering wheel?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,b:Overcorrect immediately.,c:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is usually the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain traction without overcorrecting.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:It is more likely to be raining at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: Night driving is harder because you can see less of the road and potential hazards. Headlights only illuminate a limited distance, so you must reduce your speed and increase following distance to ensure you can stop within the area you can see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the correct merging technique?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when a gap is available.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the highway, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic or a control device (like a stop sign) requires it.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.,b:They are marked with black-and-white signs.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.
note: Work zones can be stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as striping or mowing operations). They are marked with orange signs and often reduced speed limits. Drivers must slow down when required, stay alert for workers and equipment, and be prepared for sudden changes in traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If your slow driving is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, especially on a two-lane, two-way road, you should safely pull onto the right shoulder or into a turnout when possible and allow traffic to pass. This helps prevent unsafe passing and reduces the risk of crashes.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:It is summer.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work is being done on or near the roadway. They indicate that conditions may be less than ideal due to lane shifts, workers, equipment, or uneven surfaces, so you should slow down if required, increase following distance, and use extra caution.

question: A driver's license may be suspended for which of the following reasons?
options: a:Driving in violation of license restrictions.,b:Operating an uninsured vehicle.,c:Repeated violations of motor vehicle laws.,d:Any of the above.
note: A driver’s license can be suspended for several reasons, including driving in violation of license restrictions, operating an uninsured vehicle where insurance is required, and accumulating repeated violations of motor vehicle laws. Any of these can lead to loss of driving privileges, depending on state law and the severity or frequency of the offenses.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Have improved reaction time.,b:Are more aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Drive better because they are more careful.,d:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and the vehicle.
note: Alcohol slows brain function and affects judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time. A driver who has been drinking cannot control their body or the vehicle as precisely, making it harder to stay in the lane, react to hazards, and stop in time. This is why any amount of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: If you start to drive in rainy conditions, you should:
options: a:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,d:Pull over immediately to the shoulder.
note: When it starts raining, roads become slippery, especially in the first few minutes as oil and dirt mix with water. You should slow down to maintain better control and increase following distance. Turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see and be seen by others. If visibility becomes very poor, then pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:At your dashboard instruments.,b:At your right-side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas not visible in your mirrors are called blind spots. Before changing lanes to the left, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your left shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your left blind spot. This shoulder check helps prevent collisions with vehicles you cannot see in your mirrors.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Using proper turn signals.,c:Obeying posted speed limits.,d:All of the above.
note: Road rage and aggressive driving can often be prevented by planning and courteous behavior. Allowing extra travel time keeps you from feeling rushed or frustrated. Using proper turn signals lets other drivers know your intentions, reducing surprises and conflicts. Obeying posted speed limits helps keep traffic flowing smoothly and reduces tailgating and dangerous passing. Practicing all of these habits together creates a calmer, safer driving environment.

question: How must drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must always be obeyed.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that tell drivers when to stop, go, yield, change lanes, or adjust speed. They are not suggestions; they must be obeyed at all times unless a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic differently. Following these controls keeps traffic organized and reduces crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,c:Signal a lane change.,d:Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
note: When changing lanes on a highway, you should signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by quickly glancing over your shoulder. All three steps are required for a safe lane change, not just signaling.

question: Before passing another vehicle on the road, you should:
options: a:Signal only if someone is behind you.,b:Never signal to avoid confusion.,c:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intent.,d:Signal only after you begin passing.
note: Before passing, you should signal early enough so other drivers clearly understand that you intend to move into another lane. Signaling only when someone is behind you or after you begin passing does not give others enough warning.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
note: After a school bus unloads children, watch carefully for pedestrians near the roadway before resuming travel.

question: When must you submit proof of insurance to the DMV after being in a crash?
options: a:If the crash results in personal injury, death, or property damage at or above your state’s reporting threshold.,b:Only if there are injuries.,c:Only if there is damage to another person’s vehicle or property.
note: States set their own crash-reporting and insurance-proof thresholds, and the dollar amount varies widely (often $1,000 or more). A fixed $501 property-damage threshold and a 15‑day deadline are not standard nationwide and should not be presented as a universal rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Necessary only during the maneuver itself.,b:A required driving habit and good practice.,c:Required only if other traffic is present.,d:Discouraged on multilane roads.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling at least 100 feet in advance lets others anticipate your movement and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: If a transit bus signals it will re-enter traffic after a stop, you must:
options: a:Honking to warn the driver.,b:Move into the lane beside it immediately.,c:Yield to the bus and allow it to re-enter.,d:Speed up to pass the bus first.
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you should yield and allow it to re-enter traffic safely. Be prepared to slow down, change lanes if it is safe, or briefly stop so the bus can merge. Do not speed up, honk, or try to pass as this can create a dangerous situation for passengers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper top-to-bottom order of lights on a vertically-arranged traffic signal?
options: a:Green at the bottom,b:Yellow in the middle,c:Red at the top
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal, the lights are arranged red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom. Knowing this order helps you anticipate which light is next and recognize signals even if a bulb is out or visibility is poor.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for upcoming hazards?
options: a:Stare straight ahead only.,b:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and its sides.,d:Only check your mirrors periodically.
note: You should constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check your mirrors regularly. Look far down the road to spot hazards early, and also watch side areas where pedestrians, cyclists, or vehicles may enter your path. Avoid staring at one spot, which can cause you to miss developing dangers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the harder you will hit in a crash. Stopping distance increases with speed, and impact force rises sharply, which greatly increases the chance of serious injury or death. Driving at safe speeds gives you more time and space to react.

question: If you meet a school bus stopped with flashing lights on the opposite side of a divided highway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the bus lights stop flashing.,b:Turn around and use another route.,c:You may continue driving because the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.
note: On a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median between directions of travel, drivers on the opposite side are generally not required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights. You may continue driving, but stay alert and be prepared for children who might act unpredictably. Always follow your state’s specific school bus laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:At any time.,c:Only when making a turn (for example, into a driveway or side road).
note: A solid yellow line generally means you may not cross it to pass other vehicles. However, you are allowed to cross a solid yellow line when you are making a turn, such as turning left into a driveway, alley, or side road, as long as it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Be prepared to stop.,c:All of the above (slow down, look, and be ready to stop).
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop at a safe distance—typically 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail—and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the standard speed limit posted for many school zones in Alaska?
options: a:10 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Many school zones in Alaska use a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or during posted times. Always watch for school zone signs, flashing beacons, and children near the roadway, and be prepared to slow even further if conditions require.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once you have moved onto the exit ramp.,b:Slow down well before reaching the ramp.,c:Maintain highway speed while on the ramp.
note: Stay at highway speed until you are actually on the exit ramp so you do not disrupt traffic on the freeway. Once you are fully in the exit lane and on the ramp, then slow down to the posted ramp speed or to a safe speed for the curve and traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a fire hydrant is it illegal to park?
options: a:30 feet,b:15 feet,c:25 feet
note: You must not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. This space must be kept clear so fire trucks can quickly connect hoses in an emergency without being blocked by parked vehicles.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Slam on your brakes immediately.,b:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay calm, and let the car slow down by easing off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes, because sudden braking can cause you to lose control. Steer smoothly to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This helps you avoid being blinded while still keeping your vehicle correctly positioned in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why must you adjust your driving speed?
options: a:Other traffic.,b:Weather conditions.,c:All of the above.,d:Existing road conditions.
note: You must adjust your speed to match traffic, weather, and road conditions. In heavy traffic, bad weather, or on rough or slippery roads, you should slow down so you have enough time and space to react safely.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Never pass them under any circumstances.
note: Trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay visible, avoid driving right beside them for long periods and never follow too closely. Either pass safely and promptly or drop back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: What can result from combining alcohol with other drugs?
options: a:Complete cancelation of effects.,b:A guaranteed cure of symptoms.,c:An increase in the effects of both substances.,d:A decrease in effects of both.
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs often makes each substance more powerful and more dangerous. This greatly increases drowsiness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment, making driving extremely unsafe.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.,c:Copy surrounding traffic even if it conflicts with the guard.
note: In a school zone, a crossing guard’s directions must be obeyed just like those of a police officer. If their hand signals or stop sign conflict with traffic lights or other drivers, you still follow the guard and proceed slowly and carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: When your car begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This helps you regain control and straighten the vehicle without overcorrecting.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution instead of braking hard in the intersection.

question: How many points within 12 months will result in license suspension?
options: a:12 or more,b:10 or more,c:15 or more
note: Many states suspend a license for accumulating too many points in a set period, but the exact number of points and time frame vary by state. Some use 12 points in 12 months, others use different thresholds or systems, so you must check your specific state’s point schedule.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Honk to warn the bicyclist as you pass.,b:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible when passing.
note: When passing a bicyclist, reduce your speed and leave as much room as safely possible—ideally at least several feet or a full lane where allowed. Never drive in the bicycle lane to pass, and do not honk right beside the bicyclist, as this can startle them and cause a crash.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what should drivers of smaller vehicles be ready for?
options: a:Increased air turbulence or wind gusts from the large vehicle.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Loud noises that are distracting.
note: When you pass or are passed by a large truck or bus, the size and speed of the vehicle can create strong air turbulence or wind gusts. These gusts can push or pull a smaller vehicle sideways, so you must hold the steering wheel firmly and be prepared to make small steering corrections to stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but are not in the proper lane, what is the correct action?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn then.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection or a safe location to turn. Sudden lane changes, cutting across traffic, or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever stop or back up in a travel lane on a roadway?
options: a:You may stop to look up an address.,b:You should not stop.,c:You may stop to drop off passengers.
note: You should not stop or back up in a travel lane except in emergencies or when required by traffic control (such as a red light or stop sign). If you miss a turn or exit, continue to a safe place off the roadway or to the next exit; never stop in the lane to look for an address or drop off passengers, and never back up on a highway.

question: A pedestrian is in a crosswalk ahead. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the green light.,b:Honk to alert them to move faster.,c:Slow and carefully pass around them.,d:Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian leaves the crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks. You must stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has safely crossed your lane and it is clearly safe to proceed. Do not honk, crowd, or try to drive around a pedestrian who is in the crosswalk.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Get out of the car and walk for assistance.,c:Lie down and go to sleep in your car.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, staying in your vehicle is usually the safest choice. Your car provides shelter from the cold and wind, and it is much easier for rescuers to see a vehicle than a person on foot in poor visibility. Run the engine only periodically for heat, and make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane.,b:Sound your horn loudly.,c:Accelerate into the turn.,d:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Before turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk or intersection. Only begin your turn when the way is clear and it is safe, keeping your vehicle in the proper lane and turning smoothly at a controlled speed.

question: How does stress influence your driving?
options: a:It makes you less likely to fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It decreases your chances of having an accident.,c:It reduces your ability to concentrate on driving.,d:It improves reaction time.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you from the driving task, reduce your ability to concentrate, and lead to poor decisions or aggressive driving. If you are very upset, angry, or preoccupied, it is safer to delay driving until you can calm down and focus fully on the road.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery?
options: a:Drive the speed limit,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads, such as when it is raining, snowing, or icy, you should slow down. Reduced speed gives your tires more chance to grip the road and gives you more time to react if you start to skid or if other drivers lose control. Avoid sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering on slick surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A green arrow pointing left,c:A solid green light
note: A green left-turn arrow means you have a protected turn: oncoming traffic is stopped, and you have the right-of-way to turn left, after checking that the intersection is clear. A flashing yellow arrow or a solid green light requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning, because they may still have a green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or another safe location to turn around.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway shoulder.,c:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, keep going until the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Never stop, back up, or make a sudden turn across lanes on the freeway, because that can cause serious crashes.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is an open right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Brake suddenly to encourage them to pass you quickly.,b:Increase your speed to create distance.,c:Move over to the right to allow the other driver to pass.
note: If someone is tailgating you and there is an open lane to the right, safely move to the right and let them pass. Do not brake suddenly or speed up; sudden braking can cause a rear-end collision, and speeding reduces your safety margin.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition doesn't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,d:All of the above.
note: To make sure your physical condition does not make driving unsafe, you should do all of the following: drive within your physical limitations, stay physically fit and get regular checkups, and know how any medicines you take affect your driving. Only drive when you are medically and physically able to do so safely.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement in a lane mean?
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Drivers may make the movement if they choose but are not required to.,c:Drivers must stop before making the movement.,d:The lane can only be used by buses.
note: A lane arrow painted on the pavement tells you what movement is required or allowed from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. When the arrow shows only one direction, drivers in that lane must follow that direction, as long as it does not conflict with traffic signals or signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver should proceed first?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver on the left.,d:The driver who fails to stop.
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who stops first has the right-of-way and should go first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. Always make sure other drivers are yielding before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, you should:
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors and glance quickly over your shoulder for blind spot vehicles.,b:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,c:Sound your horn before changing lanes.,d:Turn on interior lights before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that mirrors cannot show and prevents cutting off another driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane to the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and check your mirrors for traffic in the lane you want to enter.,b:Check your mirrors, look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.,c:Look only in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
note: On a multilane highway, you must use a three-step check before changing lanes: check your mirrors, look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot, and signal before moving. The shoulder check is essential because vehicles in your blind spot will not appear in your mirrors.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle you borrowed, what should you do?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with the location and operation of the vehicle's controls (lights, wipers, brakes, etc.).,b:Assume it operates like your own vehicle and begin driving.,c:Conceal to the owner that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
note: Before driving any unfamiliar vehicle, take time to locate and learn how to use the lights, wipers, turn signals, gear selector, parking brake, and other controls. Knowing where everything is and that it works properly helps you respond quickly and safely in traffic.

question: What should you do to avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirror every few minutes.,b:Honk your horn just before turning or changing lanes.,c:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. To avoid collisions, check your mirrors and then turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move before changing lanes. Never rely only on mirrors when entering another lane.

question: After experiencing anger at work, what should you do before driving home?
options: a:Play loud music and drive fast to relax.,b:Take a few minutes to calm down and cool off before you drive.,c:Drive immediately to get home quickly while emotions are high.
note: Strong emotions like anger can lead to aggressive or risky driving. If you are upset, wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving so you can focus on the road and make safe, thoughtful decisions.

question: Which practice helps avoid rear-end collisions?
options: a:Watch for hazards ahead.,b:Watch for brake lights ahead.,c:Use the four-second rule.
note: To avoid rear-end collisions, you should constantly watch for hazards and brake lights well ahead of you so you can slow or stop smoothly. The four‑second rule is a following‑distance guideline, but scanning ahead for hazards is the key defensive‑driving practice that most directly prevents rear‑end crashes.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: Before backing where children may be present, walk to the back of the vehicle and check the area directly behind and around it. Small children can be hidden in blind zones that mirrors and cameras do not show, so physically checking is the safest practice.

question: Why is it important to leave a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,c:It speeds the flow of traffic.
note: A space cushion gives you room and time to react if another driver brakes suddenly, swerves, or makes a mistake. By keeping extra space in front, behind, and to the sides, you can slow, stop, or change lanes more safely when something unexpected happens.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop when two drivers arrive simultaneously, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The driver who signals.,d:The driver who honks first.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the right provides a clear, predictable rule so drivers know who should proceed first.

question: What is the minimum required amount of liability insurance coverage for property damage in Alaska?
note: Alaska requires minimum liability coverage of $25,000 for property damage in a single accident. This coverage helps pay for damage you cause to another person’s property, such as their vehicle, fence, or building.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it unsafe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only when the bus is stopped.,b:Only if you cannot see ahead for 100 feet.,c:On a hill or curve,d:Only at night.
note: You must never pass where you cannot see far enough ahead to do so safely. Passing is especially dangerous and usually prohibited on hills and curves because oncoming traffic may be hidden. It is also prohibited at or near intersections, railroad crossings, and when a school bus has flashing red lights.

question: Which safety restraint combination provides the best protection in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Only a lap belt.,c:Only an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash is using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned and prevent you from being thrown forward, while airbags provide extra cushioning in moderate to severe frontal crashes. An airbag alone is not enough and can be dangerous without a seat belt.

question: When backing, what should you NOT rely on exclusively?
options: a:Turning your head to look out the rear window.,b:Checking for moving children behind the vehicle.,c:Your mirrors alone.,d:Having a passenger guide you out the window.
note: When backing, you should not rely only on your mirrors. Turn your head and body to look directly out the rear window and check around the vehicle for children, pedestrians, and obstacles. Mirrors can leave blind spots where small objects or people may not be visible.

question: What color are guide (destination) signs that show directions and mileage?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions and mileage are green with white lettering. They help you find routes, exits, and distances to cities or services along the highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly to clear the intersection.,b:Treat it exactly like a stop sign.,c:Back up slowly if cars are ahead.,d:Yield to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection before proceeding.
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. Do not enter the intersection until it is safe, even if the light is green.

question: If the right edge line of the road is a solid white line that angles left, what does it indicate?
options: a:There is an intersection just ahead.,b:You are approaching a construction area.,c:The roadway narrows ahead and lane alignment shifts left.
note: A solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the road warns that the right edge of the travel lane is shifting left or that the roadway is narrowing. You should prepare to adjust your lane position smoothly to stay within the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do before making the maneuver?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Signal and check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal to let other drivers know your intentions, then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction of the lane change. Never rely only on mirrors, because vehicles can be hidden in blind spots.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangle pointing to the right) are used for NO PASSING ZONE warnings. They are placed on the left side of the road to tell you that you must not start or continue a passing maneuver in that area.

question: Who should wear seat belts for the most effective protection?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:Only front-seat occupants.,c:Only passengers on long trips.,d:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts provide the best protection when every person in the vehicle wears one, regardless of where they are sitting or how long the trip is. Belts help keep occupants inside the vehicle and reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: At a light rail intersection, what must you always do?
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.,c:Look both ways before crossing tracks.
note: At light rail or train intersections, you must always obey all traffic signals and warning devices, including lights, bells, and gates. Never drive around lowered gates, and always be prepared to stop when signals indicate an approaching train or light rail vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A conviction for reckless driving will generally result in which consequence?
options: a:A $50 fine and four points on your driving record.,b:A warning for the first offense and a small fine for the second.,c:Suspension or revocation of your driving privileges.
note: Reckless driving is a serious offense that shows a willful disregard for the safety of people or property. A conviction commonly brings major penalties, including possible suspension or revocation of your driving privileges, fines, and sometimes jail time. It is not handled with just a warning or a small fine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, you should:
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.,b:Stop and wait for it to turn yellow.,c:Proceed if the road is clear but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,d:Speed up to beat oncoming traffic.
note: A steady green lets you go if the way is clear, but you must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection and be ready to stop if needed.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is not permitted for traffic in either direction, except in specific turning situations.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what is the proper behavior while waiting?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and stand beside the vehicle.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Get out immediately and retrieve your documents before the officer reaches you.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer; retrieve documents only when asked.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII arrests?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only beer and wine.,c:Only prescription medications.,d:Alcoholic beverages.
note: Driving can be impaired by any substance that affects your judgment, coordination, or reaction time. This includes alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over‑the‑counter medications. DUI or DUII laws generally apply to being under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, or other intoxicating substances that impair your ability to drive safely.

question: How can drowsy drivers perform in comparison to intoxicated drivers?
options: a:Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.,b:Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,c:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsiness slows reaction time, impairs judgment, and can cause lane drifting and poor control, much like alcohol. A drowsy driver may weave, brake late, or react slowly so that they appear drunk. Coffee, fresh air, or loud music do not reliably restore alertness; the safe choice is to stop and rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must always stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:Flashing red light.,b:Steady yellow light.,c:Yellow arrow.,d:Flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just like at a stop sign. Stop before the crosswalk or limit line, look for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe. Steady yellow, yellow arrows, and flashing yellow lights are warnings to use caution and prepare to stop, not automatic stop requirements in all cases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements is not correct about driving habits and speed?
options: a:Driving at high speeds can cause tire wear and reduce fuel economy.,b:Constantly driving at exactly the same speed may contribute to monotony and road hypnosis.,c:You are required to drive at the maximum posted speed limit at all times.
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions, not a required speed. You must adjust your speed for traffic, weather, visibility, and road conditions, and it is often safer to drive below the posted limit. High speeds increase tire wear and fuel use, and driving at one unchanging speed for long periods can lead to monotony and reduced alertness.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers account for?
options: a:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,d:That trucks can always stop more quickly than cars.
note: Heavy trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. When driving near trucks, leave extra space in front of them, avoid cutting in too closely, and stay out of their large blind spots. Never assume a truck can stop as quickly as a smaller vehicle.

question: If you feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop driving.,b:Get some coffee.,c:Open your window.
note: If you feel tired while driving, the safest action is to stop driving. Fatigue seriously reduces your reaction time and decision‑making, similar to alcohol. Coffee, fresh air, or loud music may make you feel briefly more awake but do not restore full alertness. Pull over in a safe place to rest or sleep before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should your front wheels face?
options: a:Should turn toward the curb.,b:Should turn away from the curb.,c:Should point straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward and rest against the curb, helping stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Continue driving but stay out of the way.,b:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,d:Speed up to get out of its path.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

question: What is the fine for a driver who fails to restrain passengers under age 16 in their moving vehicle?
options: a:Varies by state; check your local law.,b:No fine if the child is over age 8.,c:Only the parent of the child can be fined.
note: States set their own child passenger restraint fines, and the exact dollar amount varies by state. What is consistent is that drivers are legally responsible for ensuring passengers under a certain age are properly restrained in appropriate child seats or seat belts. Failing to do so can result in a monetary fine and, in many states, demerit points on the driver’s record.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Idling in driveways with engine running.,b:Slowing down gradually when approaching stops.,c:Frequently letting the engine idle while parked.,d:Accelerating quickly from stops.
note: To conserve fuel, look ahead and slow down gradually instead of making sudden stops. Smooth, steady driving with gentle acceleration and braking uses less gasoline than rapid starts and hard stops, which waste fuel and increase wear on your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not pass another vehicle in which of these situations?
options: a:By crossing a solid yellow center line.,b:By using the shoulder of the highway.,c:On a hill or in a curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic.,d:All of the above.
note: You may not pass another vehicle by crossing a solid yellow center line, by driving on the shoulder, or on a hill or curve where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure the lane is clear. All of these situations are illegal and unsafe because your view of oncoming traffic is limited or you are driving where other drivers do not expect you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Merge to the right and continue.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Stop and proceed only when safe (same as a stop sign).,d:Ignore it if no other cars are present.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When an approaching emergency vehicle is using a siren, you must:
options: a:Speed up to create distance.,b:Drive to the nearest intersection and stop in the middle.,c:Slow down and continue driving in your lane.,d:Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop.,b:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A school crossing sign warns you that children may be crossing the road. You do not always have to stop, but you must slow if needed, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for any pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk.

question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,c:Drink black coffee.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time will lower your BAC. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; coffee, cold showers, food, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol from your bloodstream.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must drivers yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Drivers already in the intersection.,c:Oncoming traffic.,d:You must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and any vehicles already in the intersection.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic, to pedestrians in the crosswalk, and to any vehicles already in the intersection. You may only complete your turn when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be transported?
options: a:Standing on the floor in the back seat.,b:Seated unrestrained if they are small.,c:Properly secured in appropriate child restraints or seats.,d:Held by a strong adult in an adult's lap.
note: Small children must always be secured in an appropriate child safety seat or restraint system that is correctly installed and suitable for their age, weight, and height. They should never ride standing, unrestrained, or on someone’s lap, because in a crash or sudden stop an adult cannot hold a child safely. Safety agencies also recommend that children 12 and under ride in the rear seat whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean?
options: a:It is never used.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light—prepare to stop.,c:Drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow without yielding.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending and the signal is about to change. It carries the same warning as a circular yellow light: the light will soon turn red, so you should slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely. Do not enter the intersection on a solid yellow arrow unless you cannot stop safely.

question: What is the general purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Highway pavement markings provide important information to drivers. They show lane boundaries, indicate where passing is allowed or prohibited, guide turns, and warn of changes such as lane drops or approaching intersections. Reading and obeying pavement markings helps maintain safe, orderly traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn repeatedly at the passing driver.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow the pass to be completed safely.
note: When another driver is passing you, you should help the pass occur safely. Check for oncoming traffic and maintain or slightly reduce your speed so the other driver has enough space and time to pass and return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or try to block the passing vehicle.

question: What does a dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:A speed zone.,b:A safe passing area.,c:A no passing zone.
note: A dashed yellow centerline between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions means passing is allowed when it can be done safely. You may cross the dashed yellow line to pass another vehicle if you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards. Yellow centerlines always separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Go through the intersection.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are approaching and can stop safely, you must slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with caution.

question: When you first get into a car, what should you adjust first if needed?
options: a:Your rearview mirror,b:Your seat,c:The steering wheel
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls comfortably and see clearly. Once your seating position is correct, adjust mirrors and steering wheel to match that position.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drive immediately since emotions will pass.,b:Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.,c:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,d:Turn on loud music to distract yourself from emotions.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or crying can distract you and slow your reactions. Before driving, take time to calm down and regain focus so you can pay full attention to the road and drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and ensure it is safe to change lanes.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and only move into the passing lane when it is clearly safe. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and have enough space.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer travel before coming to a full stop at 55 mph?
options: a:About 400 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:About 50 feet.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. At about 55 mph, a fully loaded tractor‑trailer may need close to 400 feet to come to a complete stop, so you should avoid cutting in front of trucks or braking suddenly near them.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, you should:
options: a:Honk to make them get out of the way.,b:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Proceed only if no other cars are in the intersection.,d:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing against the signal; allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

question: What does a single dashed white line on a multilane road indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited.,b:Passing or lane changes are permitted between adjacent lanes moving in the same direction.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes across this line when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle, often with a red border, mounted on the rear of vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less. It warns faster traffic to approach and pass with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at a railroad crossing under which condition(s)?
options: a:If directed by a flagger.,b:If a stop sign controls the crossing.,c:If warning lights are flashing and/or gates are down.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when any traffic control device or official tells you to: if a flagger signals you to stop, if there is a stop sign at the crossing, or if flashing red lights and/or gates are operating. In these cases, stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, and proceed only when it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right at a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a police car.,b:Turn without checking crosswalks.,c:Maintain your normal driving speed.,d:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic.
note: When turning right on a green light, you may proceed if it is permitted, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or approaching the intersection. Slow down, check both the crosswalk and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn only when it is safe.

question: Which of these can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Only over-the-counter drugs.,b:Only alcohol.,c:Only illegal substances.,d:Prescription medications can impair driving, and so can alcohol, illegal drugs, and some over-the-counter medicines.
note: Any substance that affects your mind or body can impair driving, including some prescription medications, over‑the‑counter drugs, alcohol, and illegal drugs. Many legal medications can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read labels and talk with your doctor or pharmacist before driving when taking a new medication.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a multi-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across a broken white line when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and permitted.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,b:It only affects judgment but helps driving skills.,c:It has no effect on either.,d:It improves concentration.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain and body. It reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time, and it affects vision and the ability to judge speed and distance. Even small amounts can make you a less safe driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you block or interfere with the normal, reasonable flow of traffic, unless it is necessary for safety or required by law. If you need to drive well below the speed limit, move to the right lane when possible so faster traffic can pass.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:An octagon (eight-sided).,b:A rectangle.,c:A circle.
note: A stop sign is always an octagon (eight-sided). This unique shape helps drivers recognize the sign’s meaning quickly, even if visibility is poor or the sign is partially blocked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:
options: a:Exactly the posted speed at all times.,b:The minimum posted speed.,c:Any speed under the limit even if unsafe.,d:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions
note: You must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even if that speed is below the posted limit. Speed limits are maximums under ideal conditions; you must slow down for rain, fog, traffic, or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn right from one two-way street onto another, which is the correct procedure?
options: a:Turn from any lane as long as you finish the turn safely.,b:Signal at the last second before turning.,c:Get into the right lane well before the turn and signal in advance.
note: For a right turn from a two-way street, move into the right lane well before the turn, signal in advance, and slow as needed. This gives other drivers and pedestrians clear warning and keeps your turn tight to the right curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best approach when merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and blend with traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on-ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and then merge smoothly. Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary; freeway traffic has the right-of-way.

question: If a driver behind you behaves aggressively, you should:
options: a:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,b:Speed up as he or she is passing you.,c:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
note: If another driver is aggressive, focus on staying safe and avoiding conflict. Safely move out of their way, let them pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation.

question: After a train passes and you are stopped at the crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Cross quickly as soon as the first train passes.,b:Follow the car ahead without checking.,c:Assume no other trains are coming and cross immediately.,d:Look and listen for another train before crossing.
note: At a railroad crossing, you must not cross immediately after one train passes. Another train may be coming on the same or an adjacent track. Stay stopped, look and listen carefully in both directions, and only cross when you are sure all tracks are clear and it is safe.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:Can make turning more difficult.,b:Can increase your stopping distance.,c:Are likely to hydroplane.,d:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires are dangerous because they reduce traction. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to steer and turn, and greatly raises the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads. Tires must have adequate tread depth to grip the road properly in all conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,c:Quickly drive out and merge with traffic without stopping.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must yield to all pedestrians on the sidewalk and to all vehicles already on the roadway. Do not force your way into traffic; wait until there is a safe gap and then enter smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder to see areas your mirrors do not show.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the outside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly turn your head to glance over the appropriate shoulder to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Continue at your current speed.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or entering the intersection, and only continue when it is safe.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:When you have to stop quickly.,c:If you have lost control of your car.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of immediate danger or to help prevent a collision, such as when you lose control of your vehicle or another driver does not see you. Do not honk just because you are passing, stopping quickly, or are impatient, as unnecessary horn use can startle other drivers and create unsafe situations.

question: Which of these recommendations does NOT directly promote safer night driving?
options: a:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,b:Keep your windshield clean and unobstructed.,c:Keeping only a flashlight in the glove box in case of a breakdown.
note: Safer night driving focuses on maximizing what you can see and how well others can see you. Being aware that tinted windows reduce visibility and keeping your windshield clean both directly improve your ability to see at night. Simply keeping a flashlight in the glove box is useful for emergencies but does not directly improve your night driving safety while the vehicle is in motion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement best describes driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:Driving much slower than others always gives you the right-of-way.,b:Driving much slower is always the safest practice.,c:You should pull off the road and let other vehicles pass if you are causing a backup.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you are traveling well below the normal speed and causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, especially on a two-lane, two-way road, you should safely pull off the road where possible and let other vehicles pass.

question: What are the colors of signs indicating distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Black with white letters,b:Green with white letters,c:Yellow with black letters
note: Guide and destination signs that show directions, exits, and distances on highways are typically green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you know how far it is to upcoming exits, cities, or routes so you can plan lane changes and exits safely.

question: What type of highway signs must drivers obey?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs display traffic laws and rules that drivers must follow, such as speed limits, stop or yield requirements, lane use, and turn restrictions. Ignoring these signs is a traffic violation and can lead to citations or crashes, so they must always be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:Both drivers should accelerate.,b:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,c:The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
note: At an uncontrolled or unmarked intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:Only on hills.,b:On hills, curves, at or just before intersections and railroad crossings, and in marked no-passing zones.,c:Only at railroad crossings.,d:Only in marked passing zones.
note: Passing is prohibited in several situations because visibility or space is limited.
