You must not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at or just before intersections, at or just before railroad crossings, or anywhere marked as a no‑passing zone. Only pass where it is clearly permitted and safe.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations.,b:Directions to cities and towns ahead.,c:Parking restrictions.,d:Warning about conditions on or near the road.
note: Yellow-and-black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards on or near the road ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width, so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: If a vehicle approaching you fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward either side of the road.,b:Toward the center of your lane.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road and use it as a guide. This helps protect your night vision while still keeping you in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Still have the right-of-way to turn.,c:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but when it changes to a solid green light, your turn becomes unprotected. You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and complete the turn only when it is safe.

question: If involved in an accident, what safety steps should the driver take at the scene?
options: a:Stand in the traffic lane to direct cars.,b:Leave the vehicle running to keep lights on.,c:Walk into traffic to flag down help.,d:Stop near the scene
note: After a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, make sure you and others are safe, and if possible move vehicles out of traffic. Do not stand in traffic lanes or walk into moving traffic. Turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles to reduce fire risk and wait in a safe place for help.

question: If you hear an emergency vehicle siren behind you while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Pull over to the right and stop, allowing it to pass.,c:Stop immediately where you are.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by safely pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping until it passes. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can safely move right and stop, without blocking intersections.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow,c:Yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, such as the center line on a two-way road. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: What is the first mental function affected by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment and decision-making.,b:Balance.,c:Speech.,d:Vision.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, the part of the brain that helps you assess risk and make safe choices. Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce your ability to judge speed, distance, and danger, making driving unsafe before you feel obviously impaired.

question: An orange sign with black letters usually means:
options: a:Stop ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:There is roadwork or construction present.,d:No turning.
note: Orange signs with black letters are used for road work and construction zones. They warn of workers, lane shifts, equipment, or other changes in normal traffic patterns, so you should slow down and be prepared for sudden stops or instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ______ centerline.
options: a:Solid white,b:Double solid yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow,d:Single broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing the line to pass. You must stay in your lane and may not pass from either side, except to make a permitted left turn across the line into a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal.

question: Which is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Road signs.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night because they are smaller, often wear dark clothing, and may not be in well‑lit areas. Headlights and reflective materials make road signs and other vehicles much easier to see than people walking along or crossing the road, so you must slow down and scan carefully for pedestrians after dark.

question: On average, how many standard alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate in one hour?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:One alcoholic drink per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at about the rate of one standard drink per hour. This is only an average; factors like body weight, sex, food intake, and health can slow this rate, so a person can still be impaired even if they have had only one drink in the last hour.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Drive away if you are not at fault.,b:Ignore injuries and exchange information later.,c:Stop your vehicle.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop immediately. Once stopped, if it is safe, move your vehicle out of traffic, check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and exchange information with the other parties. Leaving the scene without stopping is illegal, especially in a serious crash.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.,b:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid red arrow means stop and remain stopped. You may not proceed or turn in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or is replaced by a signal that allows movement. It functions like a circular red light, but specifically for traffic intending to move in the arrow’s direction.

question: Which is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Seat belts are optional for rear-seat passengers.,b:You should never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag.,c:Airbags are always safe for infants and small children.,d:Children under 12 should always ride in the front seat.
note: You must never place a rear‑facing infant seat in front of an active passenger airbag because the force of the airbag can seriously injure or kill the baby. The safest place for children is properly restrained in the back seat, and all occupants should use seat belts or appropriate child restraints.

question: Which of the following are effects of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:It slows your reaction time.,b:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,c:It impairs your thinking ability.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects several aspects of driving: it slows your reaction time, gives you a false sense of confidence, and impairs your judgment and thinking ability. Because all of these are true, the correct response should include each of these effects, not just one.

question: After being involved in an accident, what steps should you take?
options: a:Stop immediately, help injured persons, and call police if needed.,b:Drive away if the damage is minor.,c:Refuse to exchange information with other drivers.,d:Move injured persons before calling for help.
note: After a crash, you must stop at the scene, protect yourself and others from further danger, and help anyone who is injured without moving them unless there is immediate danger (like fire). Call emergency services if needed and exchange information with other drivers. Never drive away or refuse to share required information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin slowing down while leaving a highway?
options: a:Once you see a toll booth.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:After you have moved into the exit lane.
note: When leaving a highway, signal and move into the exit lane first, then begin slowing down once you are in that lane. Do not slow significantly on the main travel lanes, because that can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:Assume you have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Force your way into traffic to claim right-of-way.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the public roadway. Wait until there is a safe gap, then merge smoothly. You never have the right‑of‑way when entering from a driveway, and you must not force your way into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Alaska's point system, a driver's license will be suspended or revoked if they accumulate:
options: a:6 points in 12 months,b:12 points in 12 months or 18 points in 24 months,c:18 points in 12 months,d:10 points in 24 months
note: Accumulating 12 demerit points in 12 months or 18 points in 24 months results in mandatory license suspension or revocation in Alaska.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your Alaska driver's license is suspended or revoked due to demerit points:
options: a:You can get a limited work-purpose license,b:No limited or work-purpose license is available,c:You can drive only during daylight hours,d:You can drive with a licensed adult beside you
note: Under Alaska law, no limited or work-purpose license is available if your driving privilege is suspended or revoked for point accumulation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How often can an Alaska driver take a defensive driving course (DDC) to reduce points on their driving record?
options: a:Once every 12 months,b:Once every 2 years,c:Twice a year,d:Once in a lifetime
note: A defensive driving course (DDC) may be completed once every 12 months for a demerit point reduction on your Alaska driving record.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Alaska law, a provisional license holder must complete a driver improvement course if they accumulate:
options: a:3 points in 12 months,b:6 or more points in 12 months or 9 or more points in 24 months,c:12 points in 24 months,d:4 points in 12 months
note: A provisional license holder who accumulates 6 or more demerit points in a 12-month period or 9 or more points in a 24-month period must complete an approved driver improvement course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Conviction for failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading children in Alaska results in how many demerit points?
options: a:2 points,b:4 points,c:6 points,d:10 points
note: Failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children is a serious violation in Alaska and carries 6 demerit points.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Alaska law, you must immediately report a traffic crash to local police or the State Troopers if:
options: a:Total property damage is $500 or more,b:Total property damage is $2,000 or more, or there is injury or death,c:Any vehicle needs a tow truck,d:Anyone requests a report
note: You must immediately contact law enforcement if a crash results in injury, death, or total property damage of $2,000 or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An Alaska driver must submit a Certificate of Insurance to the DMV if a crash results in property damage of:
options: a:$100 or more,b:$250 or more,c:$501 or more,d:$1,000 or more
note: A Certificate of Insurance must be submitted to the DMV within 15 days for any crash resulting in property damage of $501 or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an Alaska traffic crash is not investigated by a police officer, you must file a written crash report with the DMV within:
options: a:2 days,b:5 days,c:10 days,d:30 days
note: You must file a written crash report (Form 12-209) with the DMV within 10 days if the crash was not investigated by a police officer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Alaska, a non-commercial instruction permit (learner's permit) is valid for how long?
options: a:1 year,b:2 years, and can be renewed only one time,c:5 years,d:Until you turn 18
note: An instruction permit in Alaska is valid for 2 years and can be renewed only one time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's license issued to an Alaska driver under the age of 21 will expire:
options: a:On their 21st birthday,b:90 days after their 21st birthday,c:On their 18th birthday,d:5 years from the date of issue
note: If you are under 21 years of age, your Alaska driver's license will expire 90 days after your 21st birthday. You must pass an alcohol awareness test to renew it.
